nodes.label: Bone #fff9f3 (--color-bone)
nodes.rationale: Warm off-white section wash; white cards sit on Bone to separate without shadows.

nodes.label: Centered editorial layout (1200px max, 48-64px section gaps)
nodes.norm_label: centered editorial layout (1200px max, 48-64px section gaps)

nodes.label: Fellix typeface
nodes.rationale: Low-contrast geometric grotesque at weights 400/520; 520 gives headlines presence without going bold.

nodes.label: Hume AI
nodes.rationale: Brand whose hume.ai site this style reference was extracted from; light theme.

nodes.label: Ink #222222 (--color-ink)
nodes.rationale: Near-black instead of pure black, a deliberate softening for text, filled buttons and icons.

nodes.label: Iris #c094e4 (--color-iris)
nodes.rationale: The only sustained saturation: data bars and brand moments, never chrome.

nodes.label: Iris oklab gradient (violet to pink to amber)
nodes.norm_label: iris oklab gradient (violet to pink to amber)
nodes.rationale: Reserved for inline gradient text in hero headlines; never backgrounds, buttons or large surfaces.

nodes.label: PP Fraktion Mono typeface
nodes.rationale: Label/annotation face at 10-14px with ligatures and contextual alternates disabled; not a reading face.

nodes.label: Manim (Community 0.22 / ManimGL 1.7.2)
nodes.rationale: Rendering takes seconds to minutes before code generation and retries, and yields an uneditable video: fine for a later recap clip rendered on Vultr, not the live loop.

nodes.label: ManimGX (Manim in the browser)
nodes.rationale: ~26 MB WebGPU, 12 days old, no Chinese, Japanese or Korean text yet.

nodes.label: tldraw theme with Hume tokens and Geist/Pretendard
nodes.norm_label: tldraw theme with hume tokens and geist/pretendard

nodes.label: Geist Sans
nodes.rationale: OFL-1.1 variable font, wght 100-900 (~69 KB), so weight 520 is exact; latin subset covers Spanish.

nodes.label: Pretendard Variable
nodes.rationale: OFL, wght 45-920, Inter-derived Latin and Source Han Sans-based Hangul; wins on axis range and ecosystem.

nodes.label: Refero (Refero Styles)
nodes.rationale: Design-research library of web and iOS screens plus >2,000 AI-readable design systems exported as DESIGN.md, Tailwind v4 @theme, CSS variables and tokens; no macOS app or overlay references.

nodes.label: Wanted Sans Variable
nodes.rationale: Alternative with a more geometric Hangul (wght 400-1000).

nodes.label: Refero style for the entire app
nodes.norm_label: refero style for the entire app
nodes.rationale: When license-blocked, use geist-sans and a fitting Korean font; Manim images and diagrams must match the style.

nodes.label: --color-iris-ink #7d4fc4
nodes.rationale: (call) Plain iris #c094e4 is too faint on white paper, so marks use deep iris with a 20% iris wash.

nodes.label: PRISM benchmark paper (arXiv 2605.19382)
nodes.rationale: About 41% of Manim programs that run still fail its spatial checks.

nodes.label: Lab-label voice (uppercase monospace eyebrows)
nodes.rationale: Uppercase mono labels (COMBINED, BLOG POST, DATASET COMPOSITION) at +0.025em give a clinical index-card feel that contrasts the tight display sans.

nodes.label: Tight -0.025em tracking across the Fellix scale
nodes.norm_label: tight -0.025em tracking across the fellix scale
nodes.rationale: Anti-convention for a sans; keeps even 48px headlines compact and scientific; not relaxed at small sizes.

nodes.label: Pastel categorical palette
nodes.rationale: Pastels are surface washes and category indicators (card backgrounds, 12px dots) only, never text, CTA fills or icon strokes.

nodes.label: 9999px pill radius for actions and tags
nodes.norm_label: 9999px pill radius for actions and tags
nodes.rationale: Strongest signature: every primary action, tag chip and nav CTA is a stadium; cards keep 12-24px radii to stay distinct from actions.

nodes.label: Scientific pastel instrument panel aesthetic
nodes.rationale: A calm white laboratory where near-black type measures soft watercolor data washes; color visualizes data rather than decorating, and imagery is restrained (no photos, no 3D).

nodes.label: Shadowless scientific-flat elevation
nodes.rationale: No drop shadows or blurs; surfaces separate by hue, whitespace and at most a 1px hairline: instruments on a lab bench, not floating cards.

nodes.label: Fellix / PP Fraktion Mono license block
nodes.norm_label: fellix / pp fraktion mono license block
nodes.rationale: Displaay's trial excludes public-facing projects and embedding needs an App + Game license; Pangram requires an App license for any embedded desktop app: treat both as blocked and ship Geist.

nodes.label: Hangul unicode-range font stack
nodes.rationale: --font-sans: Geist, Pretendard Variable, with Pretendard limited to Hangul ranges so Latin, digits and Spanish always render in Geist; ~2.2 MB or ~0.3 MB with dynamic subsets.

nodes.label: Korean typography rule (:lang(ko) letter-spacing 0, line-height 1.6)
nodes.rationale: -0.025em tracking damages Hangul, and Korean has no uppercase, so Korean eyebrows use Pretendard 12px.

nodes.label: Weight 520 requires a variable font
nodes.rationale: Above 500 the browser falls back to the lightest heavier weight, so 520 renders as 600 on static families; SUIT, IBM Plex Sans KR and Spoqa Han Sans Neo are rejected.

nodes.label: Manim as optional asynchronous tool
nodes.rationale: (call) Never in the live loop; renders on the Vultr VM with a Tassel theme and lands on the board as a video card while the tutor keeps talking.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)
nodes.rationale: $4/$20 per 1M tokens, 1M context, image input, thinking always on, 'Moderate' latency: background work only, never live replies; rejects forced tool calls, so use structured outputs.

nodes.label: Gemini (box_2d pointing)
nodes.rationale: Returns [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] on a 0-1000 scale plus masks; trained for boxes.

nodes.label: OpenCV.js 5.0.0
nodes.rationale: One 13.3 MB file with findContours, warpPerspective, CLAHE, ORB, findHomography and ArUco; loaded once in the worker for geometry only.

nodes.label: Qwen3-VL (bbox_2d grounding)
nodes.rationale: Returns [x1, y1, x2, y2] on 0-1000; open weights, could be self-hosted on Vultr.

nodes.label: automata-lib 9.2 (Python, MIT)
nodes.rationale: allow_partial, symmetric_difference, words_of_length and read_input_stepwise make it a good test oracle.

nodes.label: OpenCV.js HoughCircles state snapping
nodes.rationale: Two circles sharing a center confirm an accept state.

nodes.label: One-edit fixes
nodes.rationale: Flip each accept flag or redirect each transition and re-check: under 40 checks for 4 states and 2 symbols, like edit-distance grading.

nodes.label: 3-layer voice loop (STT, tutor LLM, ElevenLabs TTS)
nodes.norm_label: 3-layer voice loop (stt, tutor llm, elevenlabs tts)
nodes.rationale: Use Deepgram instead of Whisper, and Pipecat only if cheaper in credits or substantially better.

nodes.label: Deep check (Opus 5.5 structured transcription)
nodes.rationale: Low or medium effort; returns the extracted artifact with pixel boxes, the language or regex, the intent and confidences; Set-of-Mark numbering improves the boxes.

nodes.label: domains/dfa verifier (server-side Python)
nodes.rationale: (call) Server-side so the policy and the tutor context share one source of truth; missing transitions go to an implicit dead state; reports unreachable states, nondeterminism and missing start/accept states.

nodes.label: Handwriting change detector (Web Worker)
nodes.rationale: A trigger uploads the full frame, a crop of the changed cells and the cell mask; a debug heatmap supports tuning.

nodes.label: Paper annotations (vector marks in paper coordinates)
nodes.norm_label: paper annotations (vector marks in paper coordinates)
nodes.rationale: (call) Step-by-step marks play over a frozen 'SNAPSHOT' of the analyzed frame; live-feed pointers come later; vocabulary: circle, arrow, numbered dot, callout pill, strike, check.

nodes.label: Verifier interface (pluggable domains)
nodes.rationale: Room for algebra steps and unit checks later; unverifiable domains fall back to model judgment worded as 'I think...'.

nodes.label: Microsoft Research TR-2004-91: real-time whiteboard capture
nodes.norm_label: microsoft research tr-2004-91: real-time whiteboard capture

nodes.label: Set-of-Mark prompting (arXiv 2310.11441)
nodes.rationale: Number candidate regions (ink blobs or OCR words) and ask the model to answer with a number, making pointing reliable.

nodes.label: Alur et al., Automated Grading of DFA Constructions (IJCAI 2013)
nodes.norm_label: alur et al., automated grading of dfa constructions (ijcai 2013)

nodes.label: D'Antoni et al., automatic feedback for constructing automata (TOCHI 2015)
nodes.norm_label: d'antoni et al., automatic feedback for constructing automata (tochi 2015)
nodes.rationale: A 377-student study found both counterexamples and hints helped.

nodes.label: Holding line ('one moment, let me check')
nodes.norm_label: holding line ('one moment, let me check')
nodes.rationale: The fast model speaks within ~0.5 s while Opus works, so the student is never left in silence.

nodes.label: Two-tier model split (fast live model + Opus background)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier model split (fast live model + opus background)
nodes.rationale: The fast model handles every spoken turn, holding lines and narration; Opus checks the DFA, plans whiteboard steps and writes session summaries, taking seconds.

nodes.label: Vision-flagged mistake flow
nodes.rationale: Frame diff 2-5/s, wait for pen lift, upload (~100 ms), decision gate (~0.8 s), holding line, Opus DFA check, narrated result plus whiteboard commands; waits for a >=0.6 s pause unless severe.

nodes.label: Annotation coordinate mapping
nodes.rationale: Model coordinates -> sent-image pixels -> inverse paper homography -> video pixels -> CSS (object-fit: contain), scaled by devicePixelRatio; marks stored in 0-1 paper coordinates.

nodes.label: Frame token cost and change-only sampling
nodes.norm_label: frame token cost and change-only sampling
nodes.rationale: A 1920x1080 frame is 2,691 tokens on Opus 5.5 (~$0.011): one frame per 5 s for 30 min is ~$3.90 versus ~$1 sending only on change.

nodes.label: Draw on a frozen frame
nodes.rationale: The simplest reliable demo: avoids hand occlusion and tracking jitter.

nodes.label: Handwriting change detection
nodes.rationale: No ML: a Web Worker diffs 5 fps 160x120 grayscale, lighting-corrected frames in 16 px cells against a stable reference, with a ~1 s stillness gate and at most one call per 5 s.

nodes.label: Paper flattening and homography tracking
nodes.rationale: Warp the largest bright quadrilateral to page proportions; re-align with ORB + findHomography (RANSAC) when the outline is lost; ArUco markers make it reliable.

nodes.label: DFA product-BFS checker
nodes.rationale: BFS over (student state, reference state) pairs, shortest strings first, in milliseconds: correctness is computed and the LLM only narrates; this changes 01's plan so Opus only transcribes.

nodes.label: Reading the handwritten DFA (vision to strict JSON)
nodes.norm_label: reading the handwritten dfa (vision to strict json)
nodes.rationale: The riskiest step: vision positions are approximate, so snap states to detected circles, use Set-of-Mark for labels, freeze the frame and have the tutor read the DFA back aloud.

nodes.label: LLM-written reference DFA trust rule (agree on all strings up to length 12)
nodes.norm_label: llm-written reference dfa trust rule (agree on all strings up to length 12)

nodes.label: Counterexample trace animation over her paper
nodes.norm_label: counterexample trace animation over her paper
nodes.rationale: Advance a cursor along the string, glide a token along each arrow, ring the current state; mark the mismatch and circle the blamed transition in Iris.

nodes.label: Interrupt timing via frame comparison and a decision model
nodes.norm_label: interrupt timing via frame comparison and a decision model
nodes.rationale: A sensitive frame-by-frame handwriting comparison captures changed frames and sends them to a decision model (OpenAI Decisions API) to judge whether to interrupt; pre-processing or LLM delegation will be needed.

nodes.label: Anti-goals (lecturing, constant interruption, wrong confident claims, Korean as afterthought)
nodes.norm_label: anti-goals (lecturing, constant interruption, wrong confident claims, korean as afterthought)
nodes.rationale: Failures even if they technically work, including an uncanny avatar and any unsourced statistic.

nodes.label: Escalation ladder (hint, guiding question, counterexample, step-by-step, full solution)
nodes.norm_label: escalation ladder (hint, guiding question, counterexample, step-by-step, full solution)
nodes.rationale: Climbs only when she asks or after a failed attempt; never jumps to the solution unprompted.

nodes.label: Interruption etiquette
nodes.rationale: Speak only after a >=0.6 s speech pause and >=1.5 s of pen stillness, never mid-sentence, at most one unprompted interruption per ~45 s, and stay passive while she draws.

nodes.label: 'How I read your DFA' read-back panel
nodes.norm_label: 'how i read your dfa' read-back panel
nodes.rationale: Shows Ada's transcription drawn neatly so a misreading is visible rather than silently wrong.

nodes.label: Tutor policy (decides action and timing, injects a note)
nodes.norm_label: tutor policy (decides action and timing, injects a note)

nodes.label: Vision pipeline (detector, decision gate, deep check, verifier, policy)
nodes.norm_label: vision pipeline (detector, decision gate, deep check, verifier, policy)

nodes.label: GPT-6 Astra
nodes.rationale: A separate chat model; the spec's 'astra under the hood' is a mix-up and does not change the plan.

nodes.label: GPT-6 Luna (gpt-6-luna)
nodes.rationale: The only model the Decisions API supports.

nodes.label: Jev (TypeSafe AI decision model)
nodes.rationale: $0.042 per 1M input tokens, English-first, faster in one small test (0.3 s vs Luna 1.6 s median turn) and more accurate on nuanced calls.

nodes.label: noul question type
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter's counterpart to the predicate question.

nodes.label: OpenAI Decisions API (POST /v1/decisions)
nodes.rationale: Public beta since 2026-10-06; 1-200 typed questions per request over text and inline base64 images; $0.10 per 1M input tokens with no output charges; ~0.8 s per image request in community tests.

nodes.label: OpenRouter Decisions API (alpha)
nodes.rationale: POST /api/alpha/decisions serving GPT-6 Luna Decisions, Jev, Cloudflare Clef, Mercury Decide and Liquid d1; schema uses a state array, a questions object and a 'noul' type.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Clef / clef-flash decision models
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0 27B/9B models returning probabilities for typed noul/choice/score questions over text and up to 8 images; API-compatible with Jev; clef-flash $0.05 per 1M.

nodes.label: Demo: walking through an incorrect DFA in Korean
nodes.norm_label: demo: walking through an incorrect dfa in korean

nodes.label: Mission: getting women to return to STEM
nodes.norm_label: mission: getting women to return to stem

nodes.label: Tassel (AI tutoring and learning platform)
nodes.rationale: Desktop live AI tutor with voice, paper view, whiteboard, screen share and a customizable woman tutor.

nodes.label: Accessibility (captions, keyboard shortcuts, reduced motion, WCAG AA)
nodes.norm_label: accessibility (captions, keyboard shortcuts, reduced motion, wcag aa)

nodes.label: DecisionGate interface
nodes.rationale: Default: OpenAI Decisions API predicates; alternative: Vultr-hosted clef-flash; whichever wins on labeled frames becomes the default.

nodes.label: Demo script ('Strings that start with 010', mostly English)
nodes.norm_label: demo script ('strings that start with 010', mostly english)
nodes.rationale: Josephine draws a DFA with a planted q0 self-loop, Ada interrupts with 1010, traces it in split view, draws the correct DFA with a dead state, then screen share, a Korean segment and a customization tour.

nodes.label: Synthetic Desk View clip (demo worksheet drawn stroke by stroke)
nodes.norm_label: synthetic desk view clip (demo worksheet drawn stroke by stroke)

nodes.label: Choice question
nodes.rationale: Returned ~98% on a 70% coin and shifted when options were reordered: overconfident and order-sensitive.

nodes.label: Undocumented Decisions API language support
nodes.rationale: English/Spanish/Korean support is unverified; mitigation: write questions in English so only the input carries the student's language.

nodes.label: Jev image-input conflict
nodes.rationale: A beta-thread commenter said Jev takes no images while OpenRouter documents Jev image limits; unresolved here, settled in research 01.

nodes.label: Predicate question (probability 0-1)
nodes.rationale: Well calibrated in a community biased-coin test (70% heads -> 70%); preferred for 'should the tutor interrupt now?'.

nodes.label: OpenAI vision localization warning
nodes.rationale: OpenAI's guide says the model struggles with precise spatial localization and may be weaker on Korean, so the decision gate only decides 'interrupt now?' and never reads the work.

nodes.label: Multi-lingual Mode pitch (language barriers for immigrant women)
nodes.norm_label: multi-lingual mode pitch (language barriers for immigrant women)

nodes.label: Multi-language support (English, Spanish, Korean)
nodes.rationale: Applies to all AIs, LLMs and decision models; claims Jev is English-first while OpenAI's decision model ('astra under the hood') supports all three.

nodes.label: Bilingual captions
nodes.rationale: (call) Spoken line plus a smaller translation line, on by default when the session language differs from the interface language; lets the demo audience follow the Korean segment.

nodes.label: Decision gate evaluation harness (OpenAI Decisions vs Clef)
nodes.norm_label: decision gate evaluation harness (openai decisions vs clef)

nodes.label: English decision-gate predicates (diagram_attempt_complete, new_work_worth_checking, student_seems_stuck, not_schoolwork)
nodes.norm_label: english decision-gate predicates (diagram_attempt_complete, new_work_worth_checking, student_seems_stuck, not_schoolwork)
nodes.rationale: Written in English regardless of session language; predicates rather than choices for calibration; at most one call per 5 s; thresholds tuned on labeled frames.

nodes.label: Tassel intent: general live tutor, demo as north star
nodes.norm_label: tassel intent: general live tutor, demo as north star
nodes.rationale: Sees paper or screen, talks in real time, interrupts like a good tutor and draws on a whiteboard and over her work in EN/ES/KO; the product is a general tutor, nothing is faked on stage, and quality beats speed.

nodes.label: Provider interfaces with live and fake implementations (TASSEL_PROVIDERS)
nodes.norm_label: provider interfaces with live and fake implementations (tassel_providers)
nodes.rationale: STT, LLM, TTS, DecisionGate, DeepCheck, Embedder and ObjectStore each have a fake so the app is clickable end to end before any API key exists.

nodes.label: Deepgram (speech-to-text)
nodes.rationale: $200 free credit and 150 concurrent streams; short-lived client tokens via POST /v1/auth/grant.

nodes.label: Deepgram Flux Multilingual (flux-general-multi)
nodes.rationale: English and Spanish (10 languages, no Korean) with model-based end-of-turn under 400 ms via EagerEndOfTurn/TurnResumed/EndOfTurn events.

nodes.label: Deepgram Nova-3 Korean (ko)
nodes.rationale: The only Deepgram option for Korean: silence-based endpointing, no end-of-turn model, no code-switching.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs Agents (Plan B)
nodes.rationale: $0.08/min plus the LLM, replaces Deepgram, Korean STT unconfirmed, and forcing a reply needs sendUserMessage, which looks like a student turn.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs stream-input / multi-stream-input WebSockets
nodes.rationale: Send flush at each clause end (else it waits for 120 characters); multi-stream-input cancels one utterance on barge-in without dropping the connection.

nodes.label: Deepgram keyterm prompting
nodes.rationale: Boosts terms like 'DFA' and '상태' (up to 500 tokens, +$0.0013/min); English terms inside Korean speech still need testing.

nodes.label: LLMMessagesAppendFrame(run_llm=True)
nodes.rationale: Queues a non-speech event and triggers an LLM reply; queued frames drop on interruption, so vision findings live in shared state.

nodes.label: Pipecat (self-hosted voice framework)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is better, not cheaper: barge-in, Korean-capable turn detection, word timestamps and custom events; Python BSD-2 v1.6.0, pinned because APIs are being renamed (task -> worker).

nodes.label: Pipecat Cloud
nodes.rationale: Rejected: adds $0.01/min (about the whole STT+TTS bill) and does not run on Vultr.

nodes.label: SmallWebRTC transport
nodes.rationale: No third-party service but needs STUN/TURN; the docs aim it at development, and suggest Daily for production.

nodes.label: Smart Turn v3.2 (turn detection)
nodes.rationale: 8M parameters, 23 languages including Korean and Spanish, ~65 ms on CPU, on by default on top of Silero VAD.

nodes.label: Pipecat WebSocket transport
nodes.rationale: Copes worse with packet loss; fallback when UDP is blocked.

nodes.label: Female tutor voice with a choice of accent
nodes.norm_label: female tutor voice with a choice of accent

nodes.label: One Pipecat bot per live session (SmallWebRTC + coturn)
nodes.norm_label: one pipecat bot per live session (smallwebrtc + coturn)
nodes.rationale: TURN over TCP 443 for hostile networks and the WebSocket transport as a fallback.

nodes.label: set_language tool (session language switching)
nodes.rationale: Reroutes STT (Flux <-> Nova-3 ko), swaps the voice and updates captions; mixed Korean/English sentences are a known limit.

nodes.label: Backchannel filter (minimum-words rule)
nodes.rationale: Stops short acknowledgements like '네'/'uh-huh' from cutting the tutor off; matters most in Korean.

nodes.label: Barge-in handling
nodes.rationale: When the student talks, Pipecat cancels LLM and TTS and drops unplayed audio; only spoken words enter history; target silence within ~300 ms; headphones avoid echo false stops.

nodes.label: Korean turn-taking risk
nodes.rationale: Top demo risk: Nova-3 ko has neither an end-of-turn model nor code-switching.

nodes.label: Voice latency budget (0.75-1.15 s EN/ES, 0.85-1.35 s KO)
nodes.norm_label: voice latency budget (0.75-1.15 s en/es, 0.85-1.35 s ko)

nodes.label: Non-speech event injection
nodes.rationale: sendClientMessage -> on_client_message -> LLMMessagesAppendFrame or TTSSpeakFrame; broadcast_interruption cuts the bot off; send_server_message pushes whiteboard and mouth-shape data.

nodes.label: Per-language voice accent
nodes.rationale: A voice keeps its original accent in every language, so accents are offered within each language (US/UK English, Mexican/Castilian Spanish).

nodes.label: Provider keys stay on the server
nodes.norm_label: provider keys stay on the server
nodes.rationale: No provider key ships in Electron; the app holds only a session token; client streaming would use 30 s Deepgram and 15 min single-use ElevenLabs tokens.

nodes.label: Device token auth (single local learner profile)
nodes.norm_label: device token auth (single local learner profile)
nodes.rationale: (call) First run registers a device and keeps the token in Electron safeStorage; accounts are a non-goal.

nodes.label: Goals (real-time voice, paper view, whiteboard, screen share, avatar, library, memory, language parity, Vultr, keyless build)
nodes.norm_label: goals (real-time voice, paper view, whiteboard, screen share, avatar, library, memory, language parity, vultr, keyless build)
nodes.rationale: First tutor audio <=1.2 s in English and Spanish and <=1.4 s in Korean; on barge-in the tutor falls silent within ~300 ms.

nodes.label: STT routing by session language
nodes.rationale: English and Spanish use Flux Multilingual with model-based end-of-turn; Korean uses Nova-3 ko with Silero VAD, Smart Turn v3.2 and key terms.

nodes.label: Chromium fake-camera switches
nodes.rationale: --use-fake-device-for-media-stream with --use-file-for-fake-video-capture (Y4M/MJPEG) plays a recorded clip as a camera so paper view can be developed on Windows.

nodes.label: Cluely
nodes.rationale: Advertises 'Invisible to screen share'; the spec's overlay inspiration.

nodes.label: Window content protection
nodes.rationale: WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE fully works on Windows; macOS NSWindowSharingNone is ignored by ScreenCaptureKit; desktopCapturer still skips the app's own protected windows.

nodes.label: macOS Desk View (.deskViewCamera)
nodes.rationale: Distortion-corrected overhead cut-out of an ultra-wide camera (1920x1440 up to 30 fps); built in only on M4-era Macs and the 2026 Studio Display, else an iPhone 11+; Chromium never lists it, so getUserMedia cannot open it.

nodes.label: Desk View window capture (getDisplayMedia + useSystemPicker)
nodes.rationale: Apple's advice for third-party apps; no native code and no monthly alert; costs an extra click, a title bar to crop and window-sized resolution.

nodes.label: PaperSource interface
nodes.rationale: Returns a MediaStream from Desk View window capture (macOS), a fake-file camera (dev) or screen share (Windows).

nodes.label: Swift Desk View helper
nodes.rationale: DiscoverySession([.deskViewCamera]) -> AVCaptureVideoDataOutput -> JPEG at 10-15 fps over localhost; real camera frames with camera permission only; must be signed; deferred in this report.

nodes.label: Vibrancy / acrylic window materials
nodes.rationale: macOS vibrancy needs visualEffectState 'active'; Windows 11 acrylic needs 22H2+; keep semi-opaque fallbacks (flat-grey vibrancy reported on macOS 26).

nodes.label: Desktop app with translucent overlay widget (like Claude and Cluely)
nodes.norm_label: desktop app with translucent overlay widget (like claude and cluely)
nodes.rationale: macOS is the main target for Desk View; the team uses Macs and Windows, so both must run in development; on Windows warn that Desk View is unavailable and ask for screen share; do not re-make Desk View.

nodes.label: Paper view (Desk View feed)
nodes.rationale: The AI sees the desk feed, uses it in conversation, and draws over the live feed to highlight mistakes.

nodes.label: Screenshare view (app collapses to an overlay bar)
nodes.norm_label: screenshare view (app collapses to an overlay bar)

nodes.label: Tutoring session (main unit of organization)
nodes.rationale: Like a chat: AI title from the first message ('Untitled Session' at first), AI-extracted subject, dates and type; a library sortable by last activity, creation date or topic.

nodes.label: Swift Desk View helper (primary paper source)
nodes.norm_label: swift desk view helper (primary paper source)
nodes.rationale: (call) Streams AVCaptureDeviceTypeDeskViewCamera JPEG frames (1920x1440 up to 30 fps) over a token-guarded localhost WebSocket; verified on this Mac; research 02 had deferred this helper behind window capture.

nodes.label: Desktop app (apps/desktop: Electron 44, React 19, Tailwind v4, Radix, Zustand, i18next)
nodes.norm_label: desktop app (apps/desktop: electron 44, react 19, tailwind v4, radix, zustand, i18next)
nodes.rationale: (call) Context isolation, sandboxed renderers and a typed preload API as the only IPC surface.

nodes.label: Main window (opaque bone canvas)
nodes.rationale: (call) Hume is flat, so vibrancy appears only in the title strip; translucency belongs to the overlay.

nodes.label: Overlay bar (screen-share mode)
nodes.rationale: Frameless panel at screen-saver level on all Spaces, translucent and click-through except its controls; shows a mini Ada with lip-sync, the live caption, mic level and share controls.

nodes.label: Screen-pointer window
nodes.rationale: (call) Transparent full-display click-through layer where the tutor circles and points at things on the student's screen.

nodes.label: macOS camera permission (TCC)
nodes.rationale: Packaged apps need NSCameraUsageDescription and the camera entitlement; in dev macOS grants permission to the launching terminal or IDE; re-sign after editing Info.plist.

nodes.label: macOS monthly screen-recording prompt
nodes.rationale: Since macOS 15, direct ScreenCaptureKit use re-asks monthly; the system picker (SCContentSharingPicker) avoids it.

nodes.label: Over-full-screen overlay panel recipe
nodes.rationale: Apple DTS recipe in Electron: type 'panel', setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(visibleOnFullScreen), setAlwaysOnTop('screen-saver'), accessory activation policy, click-through via setIgnoreMouseEvents(forward).

nodes.label: Cluely-style screen-share invisibility
nodes.rationale: Fails on macOS 15+ by design; content protection is used only to keep the overlay out of Tassel's own captures.

nodes.label: Windows screen-share fallback

nodes.label: Cerebras (inference provider)
nodes.rationale: Serves qwen3.8-27b on OpenRouter; ~1,500 tok/s per one unverified report vs the spec's ~550; context and price figures conflict.

nodes.label: Qwen3.8 27B (qwen/qwen3.8-27b)
nodes.rationale: Open-weight dense vision-language model (Aug 2026) with tools, structured output and streaming; image input on Cerebras unverified.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs Flash v2.5
nodes.rationale: EN/ES/KO, ~75 ms vendor / 197 ms measured, $0.04 per 1K characters, per-character timings; does not normalize numbers, so the LLM spells out symbols.

nodes.label: qwen3-embedding-4b (multilingual embedder)
nodes.rationale: $0.05 per 1M tokens; lets a Korean note answer a Spanish query.

nodes.label: qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b (streaming TTS)
nodes.rationale: 10 languages incl. Korean, Spanish and English; 'sohee' is a Korean female voice; cloning from ~3 s of audio; Korean TTS fallback.

nodes.label: Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE)
nodes.rationale: Free control plane, but unnecessary for a demo.

nodes.label: Vultr
nodes.rationale: Can carry the whole backend visibly; $200 new-account credit is the only verifiable credit; Serverless Inference runs only in US regions (sea/atl/sjc); legacy free VM tier is not dependable.

nodes.label: Vultr Cloud Compute VM
nodes.rationale: vc2 from $5/mo, High Performance vhp from $6/mo; a vhp-2c VM in Seattle sits next to inference.

nodes.label: Vultr Managed PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: From $15/mo with PITR backups, 99.99% SLA, VPC-only; pgvector registered as 'vector' and enabled per database.

nodes.label: Vultr Object Storage
nodes.rationale: S3 API, no request charges; Standard $18/mo for 1 TB stored + 1 TB egress; hubs in 14 regions but no Seoul.

nodes.label: Vultr Serverless Inference
nodes.rationale: OpenAI-compatible with vector store/RAG and tool calling; 24 live models; GET /v1/models is the only consistent price source, since marketing pages disagree.

nodes.rationale: One JSON-schema pass over transcript and frame captions returns concept tags with correctness, misconception candidates matched by cosine similarity, and Mem0-style note merges.

nodes.rationale: MLH 'Best Use of Vultr' prizes are judged on a blurb; Vultr's own showcase praises projects using Vultr as the entire control plane.

nodes.label: ElevenLabs character timestamps (chars, charStartTimesMs)
nodes.rationale: Times restart at each chunk, so keep a running offset; the basis for lip-sync.

nodes.label: Eleven v4 Turbo
nodes.rationale: ~150 ms and 90+ languages but only on the Text-to-Dialogue socket; deferred.

nodes.label: Rhubarb-compatible cue JSON (mouthCues, words, markers)
nodes.rationale: Times in seconds from the beat audio start; cues sorted, gap-free, starting and ending on X; markers time the board actions.

nodes.label: Rhubarb Lip Sync tool
nodes.rationale: MIT v1.14; needs whole WAV/OGG files and its recognizer is English-only, so it is used offline for checking.

nodes.label: Rhubarb 9 mouth shapes (A-H plus X)
nodes.rationale: Maps to Preston Blair names; the 15 Oculus visemes are too fine-grained for a dot-eyed face.

nodes.label: Layered inline SVG avatar
nodes.rationale: Back-to-front layers with CSS-variable colors, gradient stops via style stop-color and shades via color-mix(in oklab); no library matches the reference style.

nodes.label: Customizable 2D SVG tutor
nodes.rationale: Skin, eyes, hair style and color; mouth swapped from a lightweight JSON of mouth shapes per word, one asset pack for all tutors; shown like a webcam feed.

nodes.label: Avatar SVG React component
nodes.rationale: (call) Skin 8 tones, eyes 3 shapes x 6 colors with larger shapes showing the iris, 7 hair styles incl. a headscarf, 8 hair colors; a ring shows listening, thinking or speaking.

nodes.label: Stage layout ('One stage, her work first': Paper / Board / Split)
nodes.norm_label: stage layout ('one stage, her work first': paper / board / split)
nodes.rationale: The tutor requests a view with show_stage(view); the student's pin overrides; the Ada tile floats top-right; captions run as subtitles; controls sit in a pill dock.

nodes.label: Wascher et al. 2015 blink rate study
nodes.norm_label: wascher et al. 2015 blink rate study

nodes.label: Beat clock (one clock for drawing and lip-sync)
nodes.norm_label: beat clock (one clock for drawing and lip-sync)
nodes.rationale: Each beat is a sentence plus its board actions, synthesized with ElevenLabs character timestamps that drive both drawing and the mouth.

nodes.label: Hangul syllable decomposition (code point - 0xAC00)
nodes.rationale: initial = idx/588, vowel = (idx mod 588)/28, final = idx mod 28 (Unicode ch. 3); the vowel picks the mouth shape.

nodes.label: Idle blinking and breathing
nodes.rationale: Blink every 2-6 s (~150 ms each), 1-2 px breathing over ~4 s, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Text-to-mouth-shape mapping (EN/ES/KO)
nodes.rationale: English via phonemize ARPAbet, Spanish via letter rules, Korean via Hangul decomposition; merge cues shorter than ~50 ms.

nodes.label: Ada persona
nodes.rationale: (call) Named after Ada Lovelace; warm, patient and Socratic in short spoken sentences; asks before telling; polite haeyo-che in Korean.

nodes.label: Beats (sentence plus narrated board/paper actions)
nodes.rationale: Each beat is synthesized with character timestamps (running offset across chunks) and emits one Rhubarb-compatible cue document whose markers fire board and paper actions.

nodes.label: FSRS-6 spaced-repetition scheduling
nodes.rationale: Rates each touched concept Again/Hard/Good/Easy from the evidence ratio and sets the due date; the next session opens with due concepts.

nodes.rationale: The scripted wrong DFA has a self-loop on 1 at q0; the verifier must return 1010 with the q0 loop as the blame step.

nodes.rationale: Every utterance, hint, annotation, board change and vision decision; feeds the library, the learning engine and session review.

nodes.label: Session lifecycle ('Untitled Session' to AI title)
nodes.norm_label: session lifecycle ('untitled session' to ai title)
nodes.rationale: A new-session sheet picks type, language and source; after the first substantive turn the fast model writes a title (<=6 words) and subject (<=3 words).

nodes.label: Pelanek 2016, Elo-based learner modeling
nodes.rationale: Elo builds 'a reasonably behaving system quickly and cheaply' but needs at least 100 students to estimate item difficulty.

nodes.label: Language-neutral concept slugs (dfa.accept-state, ...)
nodes.rationale: Concepts are stored once with en/es/ko labels; prompts receive labels in the learner language and nothing is stored in a fixed language.

nodes.label: Elo per-concept mastery
nodes.rationale: P = 1/(1+e^-(theta-d)), theta += U(n)(correct - P) with Pelanek's U(n) = 1/(1+0.05n); difficulty d is fixed per concept because no population data exists.

nodes.label: Learning engine (Elo + FSRS-6 + post-session LLM pass)
nodes.norm_label: learning engine (elo + fsrs-6 + post-session llm pass)
nodes.rationale: Fitting BKT/Elo parameters needs >=100 students, so parameters are fixed; concepts are language-neutral slugs and notes live as pgvector embeddings.

nodes.norm_label: custom geo shapes (ellipse and double-ellipse dfa states)

nodes.label: User-vs-tutor edit tagging (store.listen source 'user', mergeRemoteChanges)
nodes.rationale: Tutor edits made inside mergeRemoteChanges are tagged remote, so student edits can be told apart; driver strokes probably register as student edits, so tag them.

nodes.label: Excalidraw 0.18.1
nodes.rationale: MIT fallback, but canvas-based with 3 fonts and no font API (clashes with the design system), no native state diagrams, and no way to tell user edits from code.

nodes.label: Graphviz DFA layout (@viz-js/viz renderJSON)
nodes.rationale: Native left-to-right layout, double circles and self-loops; converted to tldraw shapes and prepared in advance.

nodes.label: tldraw 5.5
nodes.rationale: Covers everything the demo needs: programmatic editor, animateShape, custom geo shapes, attached arrows incl. self-loops, themes, user-vs-remote edit tagging and toImage export.

nodes.label: @tldraw/mermaid
nodes.rationale: No-code fallback turning stateDiagram-v2 into native shapes incl. self-loops, but states come out as rounded rectangles (UML look).

nodes.label: Session whiteboard
nodes.rationale: Always open; the tutor draws while explaining, the student draws too and the AI must see her changes; tldraw/Excalidraw and Manim suggested.

nodes.norm_label: session whiteboard (tldraw 5.5 behind a board wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Student board edits are read back from arrow attachments, so they are re-checked without a vision call; the student's changed shapes go to the tutor as image plus shape JSON.

nodes.norm_label: thin board wrapper (keeps excalidraw as fallback)

nodes.rationale: Source-available: production needs a key (100-day trial, watermarked hobby, or paid commercial); without one the editor stops after 5 s; Electron coverage unverified.

nodes.label: Lavender Hair Tie
nodes.description: A rounded lavender band (about #BF92DE) gathering the ponytail at the crown. It is the avatar's only accessory and corresponds to the accessory (scrunchie) layer in the Tassel avatar plans.

nodes.label: Closed Smile Mouth
nodes.description: A single thin curved stroke (about #6C1B13) forming a gentle closed-mouth smile, the only mouth shape shown. It is the mouth at rest; in the Tassel plan this mouth slot is swapped among a shared pack of 9 Rhubarb mouth shapes (A-H, with X for rest) during lip-sync.

nodes.label: Soft Flat Illustration with Gentle Gradients
nodes.description: Borderless flat shapes with no outlines, soft airbrushed gradients, hair built from stacked tonal bands, rounded geometry, and minimal facial features (dot eyes, a one-stroke smile, no nose, eyebrows or blush) on a warm off-white canvas. The planned SVG layer list adds brows (and, in research 03, blush and eye detail) that the reference itself does not show.
nodes.norm_label: soft flat illustration with gentle gradients
nodes.rationale: Deliberately simple and non-realistic: it avoids the uncanny realistic avatar the Tassel spec lists as an anti-goal, and its few flat parts translate directly into swappable 2D SVG layers with CSS-variable colors, as the brief's '2D, SVG drawn' avatar requirement asks.

nodes.label: Avatar Reference Color Palette
nodes.description: Colors sampled from the image: background #FDFCFB (warm off-white), hair #784645 and #4C2C36, skin #FEC5AB and #FEDCC3, eyes #452928, mouth #6C1B13, hair tie #BF92DE, top gradient #DEBFF3 to #755DC6. A warm pastel palette in which violet is the only saturated accent. The hair-tie lavender nearly matches the design system's Iris violet (#c094e4) and the ground sits close to its Paper/Bone surfaces (design-system/DESIGN.md).

nodes.label: Side Ponytail Hairstyle
nodes.description: Dark brown hair (about #784645, shadows #4C2C36) gathered into a high ponytail on the character's left (viewer's right), with side-swept bangs and two thin face-framing strands, drawn as layered tonal bands. It is the reference's choice for the hair style and hair color customization slots and splits naturally into back-hair (ponytail) and front-hair (bangs) layers.

nodes.label: Violet Gradient Top
nodes.description: Dome-shaped shoulders in a plain crew-neck top with a diagonal lilac-to-violet gradient (about #DEBFF3 upper left, #A291E2 center, #755DC6 lower right) and no folds or details. It corresponds to the top (clothes) layer.

nodes.label: Peach Skin Tone
nodes.description: Light peach skin (about #FEC5AB on the cheeks, #FEDCC3 forehead highlight, #FDBFA0 neck, #E8B092 ears) with soft gradient shading on a round face with small rounded ears and no nose. It is the reference's single skin tone; the Tassel spec plans 8 inclusive tones for the skin customization slot.

nodes.label: ghh-avatar-reference.png
nodes.description: Square 1254x1254 avatar style reference: a soft, flat 2D illustration of a smiling young woman shown head-and-shoulders, centered on a warm off-white ground with generous empty space. It is the 'Avatar style' image embedded in the Tassel source brief (ghh.md) and the reference the Tassel design spec (section 5.5) names for the layered SVG tutor avatar.

nodes.label: Tutor Avatar
nodes.description: The AI tutor's character as drawn in the reference (the tutor's default name is 'Ada' in the Tassel spec): a friendly, front-facing young woman shown as a 2D bust (head, neck and shoulders) with a high side ponytail, dot eyes, a closed smile and a violet top.
nodes.rationale: Bust framing reads like a webcam tile or profile picture, which suits the brief's requirement that the tutor appear like a webcam feed in the dock and desktop app. The female presentation matches the always-female tutor voice and the pitch's mission of bringing women back to STEM.

nodes.label: Dot Eyes
nodes.description: Two small solid dark-brown circles (about #452928) with no whites, iris, highlights, lids or eyebrows. Because dot eyes cannot show eye color, the Tassel spec keeps this shape as the default 'soft' eye and gives the other eye shapes a visible iris.
